items.title: 52222_Marshall Royal oral history interview
items.q: That was the original "Flying Home" Band, with Illinois Jacquet (PHONETIC) and Dexter Gordon

ctx.x: Right. Yeah, he had a funny idea when he left Benny Goodman, that he was going to get a 17-piece band and have them playing all the tunes like they played with Benny Goodman's sextet, and that was his format on which he was basing having a big band, so we rehearsed for a couple of days and nothing was happening fast. So, I told him to have a seat and take it easy and we got two or three arrangers in town and they worked 24 hours a day and wrote a complete book inside of a week. Had George Williams and some guys…

That was the original "Flying Home" Band, with Illinois Jacquet (PHONETIC) and Dexter Gordon and that group of guys in the band and my brother was the high-note trumpet player in the band. That's how that band happened to get together. It was strictly by accident, because his format would have never worked and it didn't work, because he was going to have 16 people playing rhythm behind he and I. I was going to be his

Benny Goodman in the band, playing the clarinet and he was going to be playing them damn vibes. It wasn't working that way at all. So, -- and I didn't want to be mimicking Benny Goodman no way, because he wasn't my favorite clarinet player actually because when it came to other guys playing at that particular time, I thought that Artie Shaw was more to my liking. I liked his approach and I thought that he was more original than Benny Goodman was in his way and I didn't want to be sitting up there, mimicking Benny…
